decision.title: Goal-driven member service
decision.statement: EPFO is redesigned around member goals rather than administrative form names.

decision.title: UX4G-first
decision.statement: UX4G is the primary design-system and service-pattern reference.
decision.rationale: The project skill identifies current UX4G as the design authority.

decision.title: GIGW reference
decision.statement: GIGW 3.0 is the government website/app quality, accessibility, cybersecurity, and lifecycle reference.

decision.title: Government credibility
decision.statement: The interface should feel like a government service that has been properly designed, not a startup pretending to be one.
decision.rationale: Trust and authenticity are product objectives.

decision.title: Account Health
decision.statement: Account Health is a core differentiator and a cross-journey recovery layer.
decision.rationale: Members need causes, owners, next actions, and timing.

decision.title: Assistant boundary
decision.statement: Any future Codex assistant is additive; the standard UI must remain independently useful.
decision.rationale: Prevents assistant architecture from replacing service access.

decision.title: Synthetic data
decision.statement: All demo data is synthetic and non-production.
decision.rationale: Prevents false claims about member records or transactions.

decision.title: No production backend
decision.statement: No real EPFO backend access or official transaction outcome is implied.
decision.rationale: The current app is a prototype.

decision.title: Priority journeys
decision.statement: The priority journeys are Access, KYC, Claim, Transfer, and Failure Recovery.
decision.rationale: Matches supplied problem research and implementation scope.

decision.title: Batched implementation
decision.statement: Early work prioritizes frontend quality with shallow-but-real functionality and later bounded batches.
decision.rationale: Preserves scope and prevents silent product rewrites.
